about.title: Monterey Park Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Monterey Park sees hundreds of injury collisions each year, with public crash records pointing to Garfield Avenue, Atlantic Boulevard, Garvey Avenue, and the SR-60 corridor as frequent sites of reported crashes, many clustering on Wednesday afternoons between 3 and 5 p.m. If you were hurt in one of these collisions, the period right after matters: insurers move quickly, memories fade, and physical evidence like skid marks or damaged vehicle parts can disappear. LawProactive isn't a law firm — we're a free connection service that puts injured Monterey Park residents in touch with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate what happened, deal with insurance adjusters, and explain your options under California law. There's no cost to you unless your case results in a recovery. Reaching out early gives your case the best chance of being built on solid ground before details are lost.

whyChoose.title: Why Monterey Park Residents Reach Out Early

items.title: California's Filing Deadline Is Closer Than It Feels
items.desc: You generally have two years from the crash date to file a car accident claim in California, but if a government vehicle or road defect was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Waiting to gather facts can quietly cost you your right to file.

items.title: Comparative Fault Means Partial Blame Isn't the End
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, so even if you're partly responsible for a crash on Atlantic Boulevard or Garvey Avenue, you may still recover a reduced amount. An attorney can help make sure fault isn't overstated against you.

items.title: No Cap on Non-Economic Damages, No Fee Unless You Recover
items.desc: California places no cap on compensation for pain and suffering in most car accident cases, and attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no upfront cost and no fee unless you recover money.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurers often use those statements later to minimize what they owe you. An independent attorney can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: Are certain roads in Monterey Park more likely to have reported crashes?
items.answer: Public crash records show that Garfield Avenue, Atlantic Boulevard, Garvey Avenue, and the SR-60 freeway corridor have higher collision counts than other streets in the city. This is a neutral observation based on reported data, not a judgment about any road's safety.

items.question: How much does it cost to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney, and attorneys in our network work on contingency — meaning they only get paid if you receive a settlement or award. There's no upfront cost to you at any point.
